sources.citation: Lienhard, Ruth and Giger, M. (2009). Document de référence pour la standardisation de la langue daba. Yaounde.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: The catalog has no record for maza1304, so there is nothing to agree with or contradict. The work describes Daba propre (Pologozom-based plain dialect plus the mountain dialect) = Glottolog nucl1683, and says so explicitly on p. 2. It is nonetheless adjacent evidence: §1.2 (p. 2) states that per Wedekind's 1973 survey 'le daba propre, le daba-mazagway et le daba-kola ont une relation étroite et peuvent être considérés comme trois dialectes' (Swadesh-100 correspondence daba-mazagway 80% or more, mazagway-kola 85%) and that 'le daba/mazagway/kola constituent une seule langue', and it names Mouc…

sources.citation: WALS Online, language 'Daba' [wals code dab, ISO dbq], source Mouchet 1966 (alt. name Mazagway)
sources.note: No datapoints for 13A-17A (tone/stress features) exist for this language (valuesets 14A-dab.. 17A-dab return 404). Confirms WALS 'Daba' is coded from Mouchet 1966, i.e. the Mazagway parler.

sources.note: Only 2 items, both literacy booklets (2004 'Dew ngǝ gaw avǝ werti tik Kasma'; 2009 post-syllabaire). No SIL linguistic description of Mazagway exists in their archive listing.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. LOT 375 (Leiden PhD).
sources.note: Nothing on stress for any Daba-group language; sec. 5.3.2: 'The Daba group is made up of six languages. In all except one (Mazagway Hidi), there is either a published phonology, or else work is in progress.' Reconstruction explicitly excludes tone and stress.

sources.citation: Lienhard, Ruth & M. Giger. 1986 (révisé 2009). Document de référence pour la standardisation de la langue daba. Yaoundé: SIL. 28 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Sec. 2.5 'Les tons' (pp.13-15): 'Dans la langue daba chaque syllabe est charactérisée par un ton propre. Trois régistres tonals..' (H, M, L + falling on some pronouns); tone has low lexical load, marks focus/aspect/directional. Explicitly covers only 'daba propre' (Pologozom/plain and mountain parlers = nucl1683), p.2: 'le plan de description qui est présenté ici concerne seulement le daba propre.' Same page states 'Mouchet, J. (1966) a déjà travaillé sur la langue daba, parler de Mazagway, de même que Wedekind K. (1976).' So NOT a Mazagway description; useful only a…

sources.access_detail: online with restricted access (login, paywall or limited view)
sources.note: Describes another variety (Glottolog bium1280). Secondhand historical phonology: Mazagway segmental reflexes (vowels, consonants, palatalisation/labialisation 'prosodies') from Gravina's database; in this reconstruction tradition tone is set aside, so at most a remark on whether the Mazagway source data are tone-marked is to be expected. Not a first-hand tone description. Basis: Google Books snippet + Crossref record.
